questions.question: In the carbonyl group (>C=O), the carbon atom is hybridized as:

options.A: sp² with trigonal planar geometry and a bond angle of approximately 120°

questions.explanation: The carbonyl carbon forms three σ bonds (sp² hybridized) and one π bond via unhybridized 2p-2p lateral overlap, creating a planar 120° geometry.

questions.question: Aldehydes and ketones undergo nucleophilic addition reactions primarily because:

options.A: The electronegative oxygen atom polarizes the carbonyl π-bond (>C^δ⁺=O^δ⁻), rendering the carbon atom strongly electrophilic

questions.explanation: Electronegativity difference creates a positive partial charge (δ+) on the carbonyl carbon, making it vulnerable to attack by nucleophiles.

questions.question: Why are aldehydes generally more reactive than ketones toward nucleophilic addition?

options.A: Aldehydes experience less steric hindrance and have only one electron-donating alkyl group diminishing the electrophilic δ+ on carbon
options.C: Aldehydes have double bonds while ketones do not

questions.explanation: Two alkyl groups in ketones cause greater steric congestion around the transition state and supply +I electron density, reducing electrophilicity.

questions.question: In the reaction of an aldehyde or ketone with hydrogen cyanide (HCN) to form a cyanohydrin, the nucleophile that attacks the carbonyl carbon is:
questions.explanation: Base deprotonates HCN to generate the powerful nucleophile CN⁻, which attacks the carbonyl carbon in the rate-determining step.

questions.question: Aldehydes and methyl ketones form solid crystalline bisulfite adducts when shaken with saturated sodium bisulfite (NaHSO₃). This reaction is widely used to:

options.A: Purify and separate carbonyl compounds from non-carbonyl mixtures

questions.explanation: The bisulfite crystalline adduct precipitates cleanly; upon filtering and warming with dilute acid or base, pure carbonyl compound is regenerated.

questions.question: Brady's Reagent, which forms bright yellow/orange crystalline precipitates with aldehydes and ketones, is chemically:
questions.explanation: 2,4-DNP condenses with carbonyl groups to eliminate water and form brightly colored 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazone crystals with sharp melting points.

questions.question: The Aldol Condensation reaction requires that the reacting aldehyde or ketone must possess at least one:
questions.explanation: Dilute base removes an acidic α-hydrogen to form a resonance-stabilized enolate ion, which then nucleophilically attacks another carbonyl molecule.

questions.question: When acetaldehyde (ethanal) is warmed with dilute aqueous NaOH, the aldol addition product formed is:
questions.explanation: 2 CH₃CHO xrightarrow{dil. NaOH} CH₃-CH(OH)-CH₂-CHO (3-hydroxybutanal). Upon heating, it dehydrates to crotonaldehyde (but-2-enal).

questions.question: Which of the following aldehydes lacks an α-hydrogen atom and therefore undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction (self oxidation-reduction / disproportionation) in 50% concentrated NaOH?
questions.explanation: Aldehydes with no α-hydrogen cannot form enolates; under 50% alkali, one molecule is reduced to alcohol while the other is oxidized to carboxylate.

questions.question: What are the products when formaldehyde undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction in concentrated alkali?
questions.explanation: 2 HCHO + NaOH → CH₃OH (reduced alcohol) + HCOONa (oxidized salt).

questions.question: Tollens' Test (Silver Mirror Test) utilizes ammoniacal silver nitrate solution [Ag(NH₃)₂]⁺. A positive test producing a gleaming silver mirror on the glass wall indicates the presence of:

options.A: An aldehyde (which reduces Ag⁺ to metallic silver Ag⁰)

questions.explanation: Aldehydes are easily oxidized to carboxylates by mild Tollens' reagent, reducing [Ag(NH₃)₂]⁺ into a mirror of metallic silver.

questions.question: Fehling's solution consists of Fehling A (aqueous CuSO₄) and Fehling B (alkaline sodium potassium tartrate / Rochelle salt). A positive reaction with aliphatic aldehydes gives:

options.A: A red precipitate of cuprous oxide (Cu₂O)

questions.explanation: R-CHO + 2 Cu²⁺ + 5 OH⁻ → R-COO⁻ + Cu₂O↓ (brick red ppt) + 3 H₂O. Ketones and aromatic aldehydes do not reduce Fehling's solution.

questions.question: Which of the following compounds gives a positive Iodoform test (yellow precipitate of CHI₃ with I₂/NaOH)?
questions.explanation: A positive iodoform test requires a methyl carbonyl (CH₃-C=O) or a methyl carbinol [CH₃-CH(OH)-] group.

questions.question: In the Clemmensen reduction, a carbonyl group (>C=O) is reduced directly to a methylene group (>CH₂) by heating with:

options.A: Zinc amalgam (Zn-Hg) and concentrated hydrochloric acid
options.B: Hydrazine and KOH in ethylene glycol

questions.explanation: Clemmensen reduction converts aldehydes/ketones to alkanes using Zn(Hg) + conc. HCl under strongly acidic conditions.

questions.question: In the Wolff-Kishner reduction, aldehydes and ketones are reduced to alkanes under strongly basic conditions using:

options.A: Hydrazine (NH₂NH₂) and KOH in hot ethylene glycol

questions.explanation: The hydrazone intermediate decomposes in the presence of strong base and high-boiling solvent at ~200°C, liberating N₂ gas and forming the hydrocarbon.

questions.question: Formalin, an aqueous solution widely used to preserve biological specimens and embalm tissues, contains approximately:

options.A: 37% to 40% Formaldehyde (methanal) in water with ~10% methanol stabilizer

questions.explanation: Commercial formalin is 37-40% aqueous formaldehyde stabilized with 8-10% methanol to prevent precipitation of insoluble paraformaldehyde polymer.

questions.question: Reaction of an aldehyde with one mole of an alcohol in dry HCl gas yields an unstable:
questions.explanation: R-CHO + R'OH ⇌ R-CH(OH)(OR') (hemiacetal). Addition of a second mole of alcohol yields a stable acetal [R-CH(OR')₂].

questions.question: What is the systematic IUPAC name for CH₃-CO-CH₂-CH(CH₃)₂?
questions.explanation: The 5-carbon ketone chain is numbered from the right to give the carbonyl carbon the lowest locant: C-2 carbonyl, C-4 methyl (4-methyl-2-pentanone).

questions.question: Which of the following reagents selectively reduces aldehydes and ketones to alcohols without reducing carbon-carbon double bonds, esters, or carboxylic acids?
questions.explanation: NaBH₄ is a mild, selective hydride reducing agent that reduces aldehydes to 1° alcohols and ketones to 2° alcohols, leaving esters/acids/alkenes untouched.

questions.question: Urotropine (hexamethylenetetramine, (CH₂)₆N₄), an internal urinary antiseptic and precursor to the military explosive RDX, is synthesized by condensing formaldehyde with:
questions.explanation: 6 HCHO + 4 NH₃ → (CH₂)₆N₄ (urotropine) + 6 H₂O.

questions.question: Dry distillation of calcium acetate [(CH₃COO)₂Ca] produces which volatile liquid product?
questions.explanation: (CH₃COO)₂Ca xrightarrow{\Delta} CH₃-CO-CH₃ + CaCO₃ (pyrolysis of calcium carboxylates).

questions.question: Dry distillation of an equimolar mixture of calcium acetate and calcium formate yields:
questions.explanation: (CH₃COO)₂Ca + (HCOO)₂Ca xrightarrow{\Delta} 2 CH₃CHO + 2 CaCO₃.

questions.question: The condensation product formed by the reaction of an aldehyde or ketone with hydroxylamine (NH₂OH) is called an:
questions.explanation: >C=O + H₂N-OH → >C=N-OH (oxime) + H₂O.

questions.question: Schiff's Reagent is prepared by decolorizing rosaniline hydrochloride (fuchsine) dye with sulfur dioxide (SO₂). A restored magenta/pink color confirms:
questions.explanation: Aldehydes immediately restore the pink/magenta color of Schiff's reagent without heating; ketones do not react or react very sluggishly.

questions.question: Benedict's solution, used in clinical pathology to detect reducing sugars (glucose) in diabetic urine, contains:

options.A: CuSO₄, sodium citrate, and sodium carbonate in alkaline aqueous solution

questions.explanation: Benedict's reagent stabilizes Cu²⁺ with citrate ions in Na₂CO₃ solution, forming a red Cu₂O precipitate upon boiling with reducing sugars (aldehydes).

questions.question: In the crossed aldol condensation between benzaldehyde (C₆H₅CHO) and acetaldehyde (CH₃CHO) in dilute NaOH (Claisen-Schmidt reaction), the dehydrated product formed is:
questions.explanation: Acetaldehyde enolate attacks benzaldehyde: C₆H₅CHO + CH₃CHO → C₆H₅CH(OH)CH₂CHO → C₆H₅-CH=CH-CHO (cinnamaldehyde).

questions.question: Paraformaldehyde is an insoluble white solid formed by the spontaneous polymerization of concentrated aqueous formaldehyde on standing. It is a:
questions.explanation: Paraformaldehyde is a linear polymer of formaldehyde that regenerates gaseous formaldehyde upon gentle heating.

questions.question: Trioxane (metaformaldehyde) is a cyclic trimer of formaldehyde with the formula:
questions.explanation: Distilling 50% aqueous formaldehyde with dilute H₂SO₄ yields crystalline cyclic trioxane [(CH₂O)₃].

questions.question: Paraldehyde, a historic hypnotic and sedative medicine, is a cyclic trimer formed by treating acetaldehyde with traces of concentrated sulfuric acid. Its formula is:
questions.explanation: 3 CH₃CHO xrightarrow{trace conc. H₂SO₄, 25°C} (CH₃CHO)₃ (paraldehyde, a six-membered cyclic ether trioxane derivative).

questions.question: Why does acetone not reduce Tollens' reagent or Fehling's solution?

options.A: Oxidation of ketones requires breaking of a strong carbon-carbon single bond, which weak oxidizing agents cannot accomplish

questions.explanation: Aldehydes have an oxidizable C-H bond on the carbonyl carbon (easily oxidized to -COOH); ketones have only C-C bonds attached to carbonyl carbon.

questions.question: Which of the following compounds gives a positive haloform test but is an alcohol rather than a carbonyl?
questions.explanation: Halogen/alkali first oxidizes CH₃-CH(OH)-CH₃ to CH₃-CO-CH₃, which subsequently undergoes the haloform cleavage to CHI₃.

questions.question: What is the systematic IUPAC name for Acrolein (CH₂=CH-CHO)?
questions.explanation: Carbonyl carbon is C-1, double bond begins at C-2: Prop-2-enal.

questions.question: When acetone is heated with concentrated sulfuric acid, three molecules undergo condensation and dehydration to form an aromatic hydrocarbon called:
questions.explanation: 3 CH₃COCH₃ xrightarrow{conc. H₂SO₄, \Delta} Mesitylene (1,3,5-trimethylbenzene) + 3 H₂O.

questions.question: Reaction of an aldehyde with semicarbazide (NH₂-NH-CO-NH₂) produces a crystalline:
questions.explanation: R-CHO + H₂N-NH-CO-NH₂ → R-CH=N-NH-CO-NH₂ (semicarbazone) + H₂O.

questions.question: What happens when acetone is treated with hydrogen gas over a Raney nickel catalyst?

options.B: It is oxidized to acetic acid

questions.explanation: CH₃COCH₃ + H₂ xrightarrow{Ni} CH₃-CH(OH)-CH₃ (secondary alcohol).
